one_liner: Do models and humans find the same camouflage hard? Correlate model difficulty with human search time per image.
problem: Camouflaged object detection (COD) difficulty is assumed to align with human difficulty, but models use different cues; misalignment would mean COD benchmarks measure something other than camouflage.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: per-image model error and human search time correlate only moderately (rank r about 0.3-0.5), with systematic divergence classes: humans fail on semantic mimicry (leaf-shaped insects), models fail on low-level texture continuity - two dissociable camouflage mechanisms confounded in one benchmark.
why_important: If difficulty axes dissociate, defense/wildlife applications need mechanism-specific evaluation, and 'superhuman COD' claims need re-reading.
why_possibly_novel: Human-search-time-anchored difficulty decomposition for COD is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Run a timed human search study (N=20, 300 COD images), correlate with per-image model errors, factor-analyze the divergences.
main_risk: Search time is noisy and display-dependent; needs psychophysics rigor.

one_liner: COD benchmarks have a center-and-single-object bias: randomized multi-instance evaluation collapses reported SOTA.
problem: COD datasets typically frame one centered camouflaged subject (photographer bias). Models may learn 'find the centered anomaly' rather than camouflage-breaking.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: SOTA COD models degrade disproportionately (vs a saliency-model control) when evaluated on off-center crops, multi-instance composites, and empty scenes (false-positive stress) - a large fraction of measured COD skill is compositional prior, not camouflage analysis.
why_important: Real camouflage scenarios (wildlife surveys, search-and-rescue) have arbitrary composition and mostly-empty frames; benchmark bias hides deployment failure.
why_possibly_novel: Composition-bias stress testing specific to COD is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Re-render COD test sets with controlled recomposition (offset crops, mosaics, negatives), report degradation ratios per model.
main_risk: Recomposition artifacts; use camera-trap footage as the natural-composition validation.

one_liner: Quantify the information motion adds to camouflage breaking: matched-frame video-vs-still analysis on camouflaged animals.
problem: Motion famously breaks camouflage, but the magnitude - how many bits motion adds over the best static analysis - has never been quantified for models or humans on matched data.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: for strongly-camouflaged targets, 3-5 frames of motion raise model detection from near-chance to high accuracy (most of the task's information is temporal), implying static COD is a fundamentally information-starved formulation and the field's static focus is misallocated.
why_important: Redirects COD research investment toward temporal formulations where the information actually lives.
why_possibly_novel: Bits-added-by-motion quantification on matched still/video pairs is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: MoCA dataset: evaluate matched models on single frames vs short clips, sweep clip length, plot information gain curves.
main_risk: Camera motion contaminates object motion; use stabilized subsets.

one_liner: Camouflage and saliency are poles of one conspicuity axis: test whether a single linear direction in feature space spans both tasks.
problem: Salient object detection and COD are run as separate subfields with separate models, yet they plausibly measure opposite ends of one perceptual quantity.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: in foundation-model feature space, a single learned 'conspicuity' direction supports both SOD and COD via thresholding at opposite ends (linear probe transfers between tasks with minor loss), implying the two literatures are duplicating one problem - falsifiable if cross-task probes fail.
why_important: Would unify two benchmark ecosystems and reveal that dozens of specialized architectures encode one scalar function.
why_possibly_novel: Cross-task linear-direction unification test is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Train linear probes on DINOv2 features for SOD, evaluate on COD (inverted) and vice versa; compare with specialized SOTA.
main_risk: Task definitions differ beyond conspicuity (object-hood, boundaries); partial transfer needs careful interpretation.

one_liner: Split camouflage into texture-matching vs shape-disruption mechanisms and show current benchmarks confound them.
problem: Biological camouflage uses distinct strategies (background matching, disruptive coloration, edge mimicry). Datasets pool them, so 'COD performance' averages over mechanistically different problems.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: annotating COD images by camouflage mechanism reveals strongly method-dependent performance profiles (edge-based methods fail on disruptive coloration, texture methods fail on background matching), and mechanism composition varies across datasets enough to explain most cross-dataset ranking instability.
why_important: A mechanistic taxonomy converts an appearance-shuffled benchmark into interpretable sub-problems with different optimal designs.
why_possibly_novel: Mechanism-stratified COD evaluation is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search (mechanisms themselves are KNOWN in biology, e.g. Cott's principles).
minimal_experiment: Have biologists annotate mechanism labels on 1k COD images, stratify existing model results, quantify ranking flips.
main_risk: Mechanisms co-occur in single animals; multi-label annotation needed.

one_liner: Region-core evaluation for ambiguous boundaries: scoring only the indisputable interior changes COD/boundary-class rankings.
problem: For camouflaged and fuzzy-boundary objects, annotator disagreement concentrates at boundaries, yet metrics weight boundary pixels heavily - rankings may reflect boundary-style matching rather than detection ability.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: evaluating on eroded 'consensus cores' plus a separate detection-level score reorders published COD methods materially, and the reordering correlates with which annotation team produced each training set - boundary-heavy metrics have been rewarding style imitation.
why_important: Cheap re-evaluation protocol that could correct a whole leaderboard's conclusions without new data collection.
why_possibly_novel: Core-based re-ranking audit for ambiguity-heavy tasks is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Erode GT masks at multiple radii, re-score public COD predictions, measure rank stability vs erosion radius.
main_risk: Erosion destroys legitimately-informative boundary skill for thin animals; report per-shape-class.

one_liner: COD models exploit chromatic micro-contrast that humans cannot see: grayscale and chroma-noise ablations reveal non-perceptual shortcuts.
problem: If models detect camouflaged animals via sub-perceptual color differences (JPEG chroma noise, sensor pattern), they solve a different problem than camouflage perception - and will fail when those artifacts change.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: COD SOTA drops far more than human performance under chroma removal and chroma-noise matching (models rely on machine-visible chromatic microstructure), and this reliance predicts cross-camera generalization failure - the shortcut is measurable and consequential.
why_important: Determines whether COD progress is perceptual science or artifact mining; guides dataset re-collection with camera diversity.
why_possibly_novel: Perceptual-vs-machine cue decomposition in COD is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Evaluate models and humans on original vs chroma-ablated COD images; correlate model reliance with cross-dataset drops.
main_risk: Human baseline collection needed; ablation must preserve perceptual equivalence (verify psychophysically).

one_liner: Artificial (military/textile) camouflage and biological camouflage do not transfer: two data regimes with different statistics.
problem: COD datasets are mostly biological; applications often target artificial camouflage (nets, patterns, clothing). Whether learned camouflage-breaking transfers between the regimes is untested.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: cross-regime transfer (bio-trained to artificial, and reverse) loses most performance because the two regimes break different statistical assumptions (biological camouflage matches local texture statistics; printed patterns match texture class but violate phase statistics) - a measurable statistical signature separates them.
why_important: Security and conservation users assume COD models generalize; a documented regime boundary with statistical explanation prevents misdeployment.
why_possibly_novel: Bio-vs-artificial camouflage transfer quantification is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Assemble small artificial-camouflage test set, run bio-trained SOTA, analyze failures via texture-statistics comparisons.
main_risk: Artificial-camouflage data availability; may require synthetic rendering with real patterns.

one_liner: The zoom paradox: camouflage vanishes at high magnification, so scale selection IS the camouflage problem - test scale-oracle decomposition.
problem: Camouflage works at the scale where object texture matches background; zoom in enough and micro-texture differences appear. Whether model failure is scale-selection failure vs discrimination failure is unresolved.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: with an oracle providing optimal analysis scale per region, simple texture discriminators match SOTA COD models (discrimination is easy at the right scale), so COD progress has mostly been implicit scale-search progress - reframing the problem as attention/search, not representation.
why_important: Identifies the actual hard sub-problem, redirecting architecture effort toward scale policy learning.
why_possibly_novel: Scale-oracle attribution for COD is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Grid-search analysis scale per image region on COD data, compare oracle-scale simple features vs end-to-end SOTA.
main_risk: Oracle defined via GT leaks information; careful protocol (scale chosen on held-out criterion) required.

one_liner: Matting-vs-masking crossover for fuzzy classes: measure the boundary-alpha entropy above which binary annotation becomes counterproductive.
problem: Hair, fur, feathers, and foliage boundaries are partial-coverage zones. The field lacks a criterion for when to switch from binary masks to alpha mattes, so datasets choose arbitrarily.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: there exists a measurable boundary-alpha entropy threshold above which training with binary labels actively degrades both binary AND soft evaluation performance relative to matte supervision (label noise exceeds signal), and common classes (fur, hair, foliage) sit above it while most objects sit below.
why_important: Provides a principled annotation-policy rule for every future dataset touching fuzzy classes.
why_possibly_novel: A quantified supervision-type crossover criterion is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: On matting datasets with true alpha, threshold alphas into binary labels at various entropy levels, train matched models, locate the crossover.
main_risk: Threshold may be architecture-dependent; test across 3 model families.

one_liner: Train on disagreement maps directly: predicting WHERE annotators disagree transfers across datasets better than predicting masks.
problem: Annotator disagreement is discarded as noise, but disagreement structure (what confuses humans) may be a more universal, transferable target than any single mask convention.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: a model trained to predict inter-annotator disagreement maps on one dataset predicts disagreement on unseen datasets and unseen classes better than mask-trained models' uncertainty predicts either - ambiguity is a more domain-invariant signal than object identity.
why_important: A transferable ambiguity detector has universal uses: annotation routing, evaluation weighting, and safe-deployment gating - one model serving all segmentation efforts.
why_possibly_novel: Disagreement as the primary (not auxiliary) prediction target with cross-dataset transfer claims is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Use multi-annotator datasets (LVIS/LIDC/COD multi-rater subsets), train disagreement predictor, test zero-shot on held-out multi-rater sets.
main_risk: Disagreement conflates stimulus ambiguity with protocol/skill differences; needs dataset-effect controls.

one_liner: Camouflage needs global context more than saliency does: context-radius sweeps as a signature that separates the two tasks computationally.
problem: Whether COD is locally solvable (texture anomaly) or requires scene-level reasoning (what background SHOULD look like here) determines correct architectures - but no one has measured the context-requirement curve.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: COD accuracy grows with input context radius much longer than SOD accuracy does (context saturation at ~2x object size for SOD vs >8x for COD), because detecting background-matching requires modeling background statistics far from the object - a measurable computational signature of the task's structure.
why_important: Context curves are architecture-independent task descriptors that tell designers what receptive fields are actually necessary.
why_possibly_novel: Comparative context-requirement curves across SOD/COD are UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Crop-radius sweep evaluation of matched models on SOD and COD datasets, plot accuracy-vs-context curves.
main_risk: Crop-based context control confounds resolution; use masking-based context control too.

one_liner: Cross-domain camouflage: does COD pretraining transfer to isointense lesion detection in medical images?
problem: Isointense tumors (same intensity as surrounding tissue) are literally camouflaged anatomy. Whether camouflage-breaking skills learned on animals transfer to medical camouflage would reveal if COD models learn generalizable 'subtle-difference amplification'.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: COD-pretrained models fine-tune to isointense-lesion segmentation with significantly less medical data than generic-pretrained models (positive transfer of camouflage-breaking), and the transferred capability localizes to texture-discrepancy feature channels identifiable by ablation.
why_important: Would establish camouflage-breaking as a portable capability and give medical imaging a new pretraining source; negative result equally informative about COD's true content.
why_possibly_novel: COD-to-medical transfer study is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Fine-tune COD-pretrained vs ImageNet/DINO-pretrained models on low-contrast liver/brain lesion sets across data-budget ladder.
main_risk: Modality gap may swamp task-similarity benefits; include modality-adapted controls.

one_liner: COD models lack inhibition-of-return: they find one instance and stop, missing conspecific groups - measure multi-instance recall collapse.
problem: Camouflaged animals often occur in groups, but COD models (and datasets) are single-instance biased; sequential search behavior (find, inhibit, continue) has no model analogue.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: on multi-instance camouflage scenes, per-instance recall for the 2nd..Nth instances drops steeply conditional on finding the 1st (models' spatial attention collapses onto the found instance), while human searchers show much flatter conditional recall - a measurable architectural deficit in iterative search.
why_important: Wildlife population surveys (the main COD application) require counting, not detecting one; conditional-recall metrics expose the real gap.
why_possibly_novel: Conditional multi-instance recall analysis for COD is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Composite calibrated multi-instance scenes + real herd/flock camera-trap images, measure conditional recall curves for models and humans.
main_risk: Compositing realism; camera-trap GT requires expert annotation.

one_liner: Compression halos leak object boundaries in COD datasets: an artifact audit of whether benchmarks are accidentally easy.
problem: JPEG compression creates ringing/blocking artifacts that differ between smooth animal bodies and textured backgrounds, potentially outlining 'camouflaged' objects with machine-visible halos.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: COD datasets contain compression-artifact gradients along object boundaries detectable by simple filters, models exploit them (performance drops on re-compressed or raw-recaptured versions), and artifact strength correlates with reported per-image accuracy - part of COD performance is compression forensics.
why_important: Determines whether benchmark difficulty is real; parallels found in deepfake detection where compression artifacts dominated (KNOWN phenomenon in that field).
why_possibly_novel: Compression-forensic audit of COD specifically is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Measure boundary-aligned artifact energy across COD datasets; re-evaluate models on artifact-normalized versions.
main_risk: Re-compression changes many things at once; include artifact-matched control regions.

one_liner: Humans improve on camouflage with viewing time; models are anytime-flat: the missing iterative-inference dimension.
problem: Human camouflage-breaking is a temporal process (seconds of scrutiny), while feedforward models emit one answer. Whether iterative computation (recurrence, diffusion steps, TTA loops) recovers the human time-accuracy curve shape is unexplored.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: model families with iterative inference show accuracy-vs-compute curves qualitatively matching human time-accuracy curves on COD (log-linear gains), while feedforward models are flat - and the iterative gains concentrate on exactly the images where humans need long viewing, suggesting shared computational structure in the search process.
why_important: Connects camouflage perception to a concrete computational property (iterative refinement) with architecture-agnostic evidence.
why_possibly_novel: Time-accuracy curve matching between humans and iterative models on COD is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Collect human time-accuracy data (masked-exposure protocol); run diffusion/recurrent segmenters at varying step counts; compare curve families per image.
main_risk: Curve similarity is weak evidence for mechanism sharing; frame claims carefully.

one_liner: Background-statistics complexity predicts COD difficulty better than any object property: difficulty lives in the scene, not the animal.
problem: COD difficulty is intuitively attributed to the animal's camouflage quality, but the background's statistical richness (how many plausible hiding textures it offers) may dominate.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: per-image model error is predicted more strongly by background texture-diversity statistics (entropy of local texture descriptors) than by object-side features (size, contrast, edge density), and manipulating backgrounds alone (same animal composited into richer scenes) moves difficulty as predicted - difficulty is a scene property.
why_important: Difficulty prediction from unlabeled scenes enables dataset design, active collection, and deployment risk maps (which habitats defeat detection).
why_possibly_novel: Scene-side difficulty attribution with compositing causality is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Regress errors on scene vs object features across COD datasets; run compositing intervention study.
main_risk: Compositing artifacts alter difficulty independently; needs artifact-controlled composites.

one_liner: Part-level ambiguity in camouflage: where the animal ends and the mimicked substrate begins is sometimes objectively undecidable - propose decision-theoretic annotation.
problem: A stick insect's legs against twigs create regions where even experts cannot delimit the boundary (occlusion + mimicry). Forcing binary annotation there manufactures noise that training and evaluation both inherit.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: expert annotators given an explicit 'undecidable' label option use it on a stable, reproducible subset of pixels (high inter-expert agreement on WHERE decisions are impossible), and excluding those regions from training improves model performance on the decidable majority - undecidability is itself reliably annotatable.
why_important: Introduces a third label state with measurable reliability, applicable to every ambiguity-heavy domain (medical margins, smoke edges).
why_possibly_novel: Reproducibility measurement of explicit undecidability annotation is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Three-state re-annotation of 300 hard COD images by 5 experts, measure agreement on the undecidable state, retrain with exclusion masks.
main_risk: Annotators may use the escape hatch inconsistently without strict protocol; instructions design is critical.

one_liner: Eulerian micro-motion amplification as COD preprocessing: breathing and heartbeat make hidden animals visible to ordinary segmenters.
problem: Living camouflaged animals exhibit involuntary micro-motions invisible per-frame. Motion amplification could convert the temporal signal into spatial signal that any static model can use - untested as a COD pipeline.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: applying temporal motion amplification to static-camera clips converts a substantial fraction of model-undetectable camouflaged animals into detectable ones at fixed false-positive rate, with gains concentrated on live-and-still subjects (validating the biological mechanism).
why_important: A cheap, model-agnostic capability jump for wildlife monitoring and search applications, grounded in a physical signal orthogonal to appearance.
why_possibly_novel: Motion-magnification preprocessing for COD is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search (magnification itself is KNOWN: Eulerian Video Magnification, Wu et al. 2012).
minimal_experiment: Fixed-camera wildlife clips with hidden animals: run detection with and without amplification preprocessing at matched FPR.
main_risk: Wind-driven vegetation motion amplifies too; needs frequency-band selection tuned to biological motion.

one_liner: Findability bias: COD datasets contain only camouflage that FAILED (someone photographed it) - true camouflage performance is unbounded above benchmarks.
problem: Every COD image exists because a human found the animal. Camouflage that succeeds is systematically absent from data, meaning benchmarks sample the easy tail of the true distribution - an unmeasurable-seeming selection bias that can actually be bounded.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: using camera-trap archives where animal presence is known independently (telemetry-collared animals, baited sites with activity logs), the recall of both humans and models on 'present-but-unphotographable' cases is drastically lower than benchmark numbers - and the gap (findability bias magnitude) can be estimated quantitatively for the first time.
why_important: All COD performance claims inherit this bias; measuring it converts an epistemological worry into a correction factor for real-world deployment planning.
why_possibly_novel: Independent-presence-verified COD evaluation is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Partner with ecology telemetry datasets: sample camera-trap frames where collar GPS confirms in-view presence, measure detection rates vs standard benchmarks.
main_risk: GPS-to-camera-frame alignment uncertainty; requires ecology collaboration and careful geometry.

one_liner: Boundary-gradient-direction statistics separate camouflaged from conspicuous objects: a low-level signature of camouflage strategy.
problem: Camouflaged boundaries should have systematically weaker and differently-oriented image gradients than normal object boundaries, but this low-level statistical characterization of camouflage has not been built - it could ground difficulty measures and detection priors in measurable image structure.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: the joint distribution of (gradient magnitude, gradient-to-boundary-normal angle) along GT boundaries cleanly separates camouflaged from conspicuous objects, and the separation axis predicts per-object model failure better than global contrast measures - camouflage has a quantitative boundary signature.
why_important: Provides an image-computable camouflage-strength scale (useful for dataset design, difficulty stratification, and even camouflage design/assessment in biology).
why_possibly_novel: Boundary-statistics-based camouflage quantification is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Compute the joint statistics on COD vs COCO boundaries, train a difficulty predictor, validate against per-object model errors.
main_risk: Statistic may reduce to known contrast measures; the angular component is the novelty bet.

one_liner: Shadow inconsistency betrays camouflaged objects: texture can mimic, but cast shadows obey geometry that mimicry cannot fake.
problem: An animal matching background texture still casts a body-shaped shadow inconsistent with flat substrate. Shadow-based camouflage-breaking is documented in biology (countershading counters it) but unused in computational COD.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: explicit shadow-geometry analysis (detecting shadow regions inconsistent with local surface relief implied by the rest of the scene) detects a meaningful subset of camouflaged objects that texture-based models miss entirely, and the two detection channels' errors are near-independent (large ensemble gain).
why_important: An orthogonal physical channel with near-independent errors is the most valuable kind of ensemble component for high-stakes search.
why_possibly_novel: Shadow-consistency reasoning for COD is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Annotate shadow evidence on COD subsets with strong directional light, build shadow-anomaly detector, measure complementary recall.
main_risk: Only works under directional lighting; diffuse-light scenes contribute nothing (operating-envelope caveat).

one_liner: Human-AI teaming for camouflage search: model proposals + human verification exceeds either alone, but only if model uncertainty is exposed.
problem: COD applications are human-in-the-loop (rangers, searchers), yet benchmarks evaluate models solo. Team performance - and what model outputs (masks, heatmaps, uncertainty) maximize it - is unmeasured.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: showing calibrated model heatmaps (not binary masks) roughly doubles human search efficiency on hard camouflage while binary masks INDUCE misses via anchoring (humans stop searching after verifying shown proposals) - output format causally changes team recall, with binary masks the worst choice despite being the field's standard output.
why_important: The deliverable format question affects every deployed search system; anchoring-induced misses are a safety-relevant human-factors failure invisible to model-only evaluation.
why_possibly_novel: Output-format causal study for camouflage search teaming is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Controlled search study (N=30) with format conditions (none/mask/heatmap/uncertainty), measure team recall, time, and anchoring miss rates.
main_risk: Human-subject logistics; effects may depend on searcher expertise (recruit both novices and experts).

one_liner: Model-specific worst-case camouflage synthesis: use texture generation to find each model's blind spots and test whether blindness transfers.
problem: COD evaluates on nature's camouflage, but each model has its own worst-case textures. Whether adversarially-synthesized camouflage transfers across models would reveal if camouflage vulnerability is architectural or universal.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: per-model optimized camouflage textures (differentiable rendering of object surface texture against fixed backgrounds) reduce that model's detection to near zero while remaining human-detectable, and transfer across model families at rates well below adversarial-perturbation transfer - camouflage blind spots are model-specific, unlike pixel-attack vulnerability.
why_important: Maps the difference between perceptual camouflage (universal) and model camouflage (idiosyncratic), with defense implications for anyone relying on automated detection.
why_possibly_novel: Cross-model transferability analysis of synthesized 3D-consistent camouflage is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search (adversarial texture work is KNOWN, e.g. adversarial patches/clothing).
minimal_experiment: Optimize textures against 3 detector families in simulation, cross-evaluate the transfer matrix, verify human-visibility with a small study.
main_risk: Simulation-optimized textures may not survive real rendering conditions; physical validation is a larger follow-up.

one_liner: Ambiguous boundaries drift with image resolution: the same object gets objectively different 'correct' boundaries at different scales - boundary GT is scale-relative.
problem: A fuzzy boundary annotated at 4K differs from the same boundary annotated at 512px, not by error but by information availability. Datasets mix annotation scales silently, and evaluation assumes scale-absolute GT.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: annotator boundary placement on ambiguous edges shifts systematically (not just noisily) with viewing resolution - a measurable scale-dependent bias field - and models trained on mixed-resolution annotations learn an average boundary that is optimal at NO resolution, degrading boundary metrics at every scale.
why_important: Establishes that boundary ground truth is scale-relative, forcing resolution metadata into annotation protocols and scale-conditional evaluation - a foundational correction for boundary research.
why_possibly_novel: Scale-relativity of boundary annotation as a measured phenomenon is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Have annotators label identical fuzzy boundaries at 4 zoom levels (order-randomized), quantify systematic placement shifts vs noise.
main_risk: Zoom interfaces confound with interaction affordances (brush size); strict interface control needed.
